title: Phase switching in real life: a 25 A home and an 80 A car dealership
description: Two measured examples of VOOL phase switching: a private home with two EVs behind a 25 A fuse, and eight chargers behind 80 A at United Motors.
markdown:
Most buildings have more grid capacity than they use. The catch is that it sits on three separate phases, and the phases are rarely loaded evenly. A single-phase car that happens to charge on the busiest phase can push that phase to its limit while the other two stand half empty.

Ordinary load balancing can only do one thing about that: slow the chargers down. VOOL does something else. The VOOL LMC measures all three phases at the grid connection and moves a single-phase car to the phase with the most room. We call this phase switching. It is patented, and it works in every VOOL Charger that has an LMC.

Below are two measured examples from the LMC logs: a private home and a commercial site.

## A home with two EVs behind a 25 A fuse

A house near Tallinn has two VOOL Chargers, a VOOL LMC and a 25 A main fuse. Two electric cars charge there.

One phase of a 25 A connection carries about 5.8 kW. If both cars had to share one phase, that would be all the charging power the house has. When each car gets its own phase, the whole connection goes to work: about 17 kW across three phases.

![Usable charging power behind a 25 A main fuse: 5.8 kW on one phase, 17 kW on all three](/img/news/phase-switching-home-en.webp)

What the logs show:

- **55 automatic phase switches in 10 weeks.** Nobody touched the chargers; the LMC moved the cars as the house load changed.
- **39 A of charging at the same time, on different phases.** That is 156% of what one 25 A phase can carry, so both cars charged at full speed.
- **Phase imbalance fell from 138% to 84% on average.**
- **739 charging sessions and 4.4 MWh in 12 months**, all behind the same 25 A fuse.

## Eight chargers behind 80 A at United Motors

United Motors at Reti tee 4 in Tallinn has eight VOOL Chargers and one VOOL LMC behind an 80 A main fuse.

On 11 November 2026 a single-phase car was charging on phase L3, which was carrying 61 A. At 10:31 a three-phase car started on another charger and added 15 A to every phase. Left alone, L3 would have reached 77 A, which is 96% of the connection.

The LMC moved the single-phase car from L3 to L2. Charging paused for 14 seconds, and within a few minutes the car was back at 15 A. Both cars charged at full current and no phase went above 61 A.

![Grid current per phase at United Motors on 11 November 2026: before, without phase switching (calculated) and with phase switching (measured)](/img/news/phase-switching-site-en.webp)

The 77 A figure is calculated from the logged currents; the other values are measured.

In the same week the LMC switched phases automatically three times (11, 16 and 17 November), and the highest logged grid current was 78 A out of 80. Since December 2025 the site has delivered 2,763 charging sessions and 43 MWh on the same connection.

## What it means for a building

- **More chargers on the connection you already have.** Capacity on the quiet phases is used instead of being left idle.
- **Fewer slow-downs.** A car is moved before it has to be throttled.
- **A grid upgrade can often be avoided or postponed.**
